ledger.claim: The trip_record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown all carry TRP-09112 and describe one continuous trip: the trace's first fix at 14:10:00 is the trip_record.started_at, its last fix at 14:32:00 is the trip_record.ended_at, and the ledger bills at 14:32:03. The rider has shown what POL-RD-08(a) requires — the artifacts describe the same trip.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 133 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage of the completed trip, no gaps, and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so none of POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) is engaged and no discount to the distances measured from it is warranted under POL-GEN-02. The measurement on this trip is the best evidence there is.

Under POL-RD-01 the governing figure is the trace, not the rounded convenience copy on the trip_record: the trace measures 11.5 km for the completed trip against a booked optimal of 10.0 km, an excess of 1.5 km driven and paid for. That excess clears the 0.8 km absolute limb of the establishment test.

The rider is straight about the arithmetic rather than stretching it: 1.5 km is 15% of the 10.0 km optimal, and POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed 20% of optimal AND 0.8 km absolute, both tests passing together. The percentage limb is not met on this record, and the rider does not assert that a route deviation is established by the 1.5 km excess.

Nothing on this record shifts the extra distance onto the rider. The trip's chat log holds exactly one message, sent by the RIDER at 14:21:40 — 'This looks a little longer than the route shown at booking' — which is a question, not an instruction: it names no road and no place, and waypoint_hint is null, so the corroboration test in POL-RD-04 cannot be run at all and the clause is unavailable. The driver's answer that he 'stayed on ordinary through roads and made no additional stop' points to no artifact and no clause, and under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight.

No traffic advisory covers this trip. The only advisory artifact in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-09112-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; the rider cites that absence, not any content, and discloses the weight as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. POL-RD-03 can therefore exonerate nothing here, because it demands an advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses within a validity window of the vehicle's passage.

Neither re-baselining route is open on this record. The trip_record shows no relocation (pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null, amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are null), so POL-RD-05 cannot substitute a re-quoted optimal; and the vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline has no application. The 10.0 km booked optimal stands as the comparator for the whole trip.

If a deviation were established, the quantum is the rider's own figure rather than an invented one. Running POL-RD-02 on the fare_breakdown, and reading the surge multiplier of 1.0 from that same artifact as POL-RD-02 requires: (3.80 + 0.75 x 10.0 + 0.28 x 20.0) x 1.0 = 16.90, plus the 0.80 platform fee = 17.70; the refund is 19.39 - 17.70 = 1.69, rounded up to 1.70, comfortably above the 0.50 de minimis.

The rider's profile imposes no additional corroboration on this claim: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 condition of 4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated is not met and the unimpaired trace measures the excess on its own. No other field on either profile is relied on for any purpose, as POL-GEN-01 requires.

Every dollar the rider paid went into distance and time on the route actually driven. The fare breakdown reconciles line by line — base 3.80 + distance 8.63 + time 6.16 + platform 0.80 = 19.39 — and the 8.63 distance line is the trace's own 11.5 km at 0.75 per km, with no ERP gantry, no toll and no surcharge anywhere in the ledger, so 1.5 km of that billed distance lies beyond the route quoted at booking.

The governing distance measurement is the length of the gps_trace polyline, and POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the field that controls the threshold test — trip_record.actual_distance_km is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may not be cited for it. The trace records 11.5 km against a booked optimal of 10.0 km, an excess of 1.50 km, and the platform's own derived block carries that same figure with status 'no deviation'.

POL-RD-01 requires BOTH establishment tests to pass: the excess must be greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The absolute limb is met at 1.50 km, but the 1.50 km excess is 15.00% of the 10.0 km optimal route, which is under the 20% limb. The percentage test fails, and on POL-RD-01's own wording both must pass.

Because one of the two mandatory establishment tests fails, no route deviation exists on this trip, and POL-RD-01 directs that the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The rider's own claim — 'about 1.5 km longer' — is arithmetically the 15% figure that falls below the gate, so his evidence proves the driver's point rather than his own.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold before the burden shifts to the driver. He cannot discharge limb (b): 1.50 km on a 10.0 km optimal is 15%, short of the 20% limb. The burden never shifts, so the driver is not required to invoke POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12 at all, and the chat log in any event contains no detour instruction — only the rider's single observation that the ride 'looks a little longer'.

The trace cannot be displaced as unreliable: it carries 133 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, no gaps at all and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, and its admissibility is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes. POL-RD-07's impairment limbs (a) to (c) are therefore not engaged, the measurement stands as recorded, and there is no data failure to escalate on.

POL-RD-02, the optimal-route fare recomputation, runs only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01'. No deviation is established here, so the recomputation never runs, no distance refund is available to the rider, and his request that the difference be refunded has no basis in the policy arithmetic.

There is no residual billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4) that could reach the same result by another route. The fare_breakdown shows an empty erp_gantries array, an airport_surcharge of 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, and distance_charged_km of 11.5 km matching the trace figure exactly — every charged line has a counterpart, so no line is refundable as a standalone pass-through correction.

NO_ACTION is party-relative under POL-GEN-03: it leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status and refund_issued_sgd exactly as they are. This is a rider-filed dispute and the charge is recorded as 'CHARGED' with 0.00 refunded, so NO_ACTION preserves the driver's metered fare of SGD 19.39 in full and moves no money against him.

replay.note: the advocates' outputs were replayed from an earlier run and not regenerated by this one: only the judge was called, so the figures here measure the judge's behaviour on fixed inputs and not the whole pipeline

ruling.explanation:
Both of you: this trip was driven 11.5 km against a booked optimal route of 10.0 km, an excess of 1.5 km, which is 15% of the booked route. Under POL-RD-01 a route deviation is established only when the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of the optimal distance AND greater than 0.8 km. The absolute limb is satisfied (1.5 km > 0.8 km), but the percentage limb is not (15% < 20%), and both tests must pass together. One test failing means no deviation exists, and POL-RD-01 itself then directs NO_ACTION however the trip is described. Rider, your own submission concedes this arithmetic, and the driver's does too; the two sides agree on the numbers, and the only disagreement was about the consequence.

Rider, on your quantum: your figure of about SGD 1.69 is correctly derived — reading the surge multiplier of 1.0 from the fare_breakdown, the POL-RD-02 recomputation is (3.80 + 0.75 x 10.0 + 0.28 x 20.0) x 1.0 + 0.80 = 17.70, and 19.39 - 17.70 = 1.69 — but POL-RD-02 only runs 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01'. No deviation is established, so the recomputation never runs and no distance-or-time refund is available on this trip.

I also checked the routes that could have reached the same result another way, and none is open. POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the fare_breakdown itemises base 3.80 + distance 8.63 + time 6.16 + platform 0.80 = 19.39, with an empty ERP gantry list, no toll and a 0.00 airport surcharge on a trip that neither starts nor ends at an airport, and the 8.63 distance line is exactly the travelled 11.5 km at 0.75/km, so every charged line has a counterpart and nothing is refundable as a phantom or pass-through line. POL-RD-04 driver compensation: the distance billed (11.5 km) is not less than the distance traced (11.5 km), so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall and no compensation is due.

On the evidence quality: the GPS trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 — 133 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds — so none of limbs (a) to (c) is engaged, the distances it records stand, and there is no data failure to escalate. The only MISSING artifact, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09112-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), was cited by the rider only as an absence, and it carries no content either way; POL-RD-03 is not invoked by anyone and exonerates nothing. The chat log holds a single rider question sent mid-trip ('This looks a little longer than the route shown at booking') with a null waypoint_hint, so it is no detour instruction and POL-RD-04 has nothing to exclude in any event. The driver's statement that he stayed on ordinary through roads and made no additional stop cites no artifact and no clause; it is not needed, because the rider never discharged the initial POL-RD-08 burden on the threshold, so the burden never shifted to the driver and no exculpatory clause had to be invoked.

The result is NO_ACTION. Under POL-GEN-03 that is party-relative: because this is a rider-filed dispute, the fare_breakdown's payment_status 'CHARGED' and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 are left exactly as they are, so the metered fare of SGD 19.39 stands. Nothing is refunded to the rider and nothing is owed to the driver. No clause produces a referral on these facts.
